name: ni-media
listed_description: C++ library for reading and writing audio files.
reason: No benchmark, speed claim or baseline comparison anywhere reachable: README, audiostream/README.md, pcm/README.md, CHANGELOG.md and repo listing (no benchmark folder) opened. The pcm README only says its runtime iterator is 'less performant' than its own compile-time iterator, with no numbers and no outside baseline (libsndfile etc.). MIT, 254 stars.

name: olive.c
reason: No benchmark or performance claim: README opened (WIP warning, 'simple graphics library', no numbers), repo listing has no benchmark folder; WebSearch for olive.c against Cairo, AGG, SDL or Skia found nothing. Single-header C, MIT, 2.5k stars.

name: OpenAL (OpenAL Soft)
listed_description: Open Audio Library - A crossplatform audio API.
reason: Listed site openal.org was not opened (API spec site; the maintained implementation is https://github.com/kcat/openal-soft, LGPL-2.0-or-later, README, ChangeLog, docs/hrtf.txt, docs/env-vars.txt and alsoftrc.sample opened). No numeric comparison against any named baseline: the ChangeLog has only unquantified 'improved performance of ...' lines. A WebSearch snippet mentions an lwjgl blog post saying SSE resamplers roughly halved OpenAL Soft's CPU use in 1.16 (OpenArena profile), but that compares OpenAL Soft with its own older version, and blog.lwjgl.org is blocked here so the numbers were not seen. Searches for OpenAL Soft against FMOD, SoLoud, miniaudio or SDL_mixer found no benchmark.

name: OpenH264
reason: No first-party benchmark: README, wiki (7 API pages), RELEASES and repo page opened, none contain speed numbers or a comparison with x264/FFmpeg. Third-party evidence found points the other way. cisco/openh264 issue #2962 (Apr 2018, opened): 1920x1080, 600 frames, single thread, OpenH264 209.7 s vs x264 via FFmpeg 54.711 s (x264 about 3.8x faster, private build, a maintainer suspected -O0); issue #2067 (opened): OpenH264 1080p best 12 fps vs x264 'up to 40fps' on a 1.4 GHz Core i5, x264 preset unstated, maintainer says the gap is 'very little' at equal quality in Baseline profile. A WebSearch snippet of a 2018 libav-user/x264-devel post reported OpenH264 '4 times faster' (54.7 s vs 13.6 s) but its 54.7 s equals the x264 time in issue #2962, so the snippet looks reversed or mislabelled; those mailing-list pages are blocked here and were not opened. A mendevi (readthedocs, blocked, snippet only) dataset page says libopenh264 used less energy than libx264 at equal resolution and quality, with no numbers seen. BSD-2-Clause, 6.2k stars.
